topic: Lesson 27: Work Rate (工作效率／工程問題)
formulas: Work done ÷ Time = Rate (工作效率)
Work rate = the amount done in one unit of time (單位時間內完成的工作量)

questions.title: Find the rate
questions.q: Oliver painted 24 fences in 4 hours. Noah painted 30 fences in 6 hours. Who works faster, and by how many fences per hour?

options.D: They work at the same rate

questions.explanation: Rate = work ÷ time. Oliver: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 fences/h. Noah: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 fences/h. 6 − 5 = 1, so Oliver is faster by 1 fence per hour.

wrong.A: You compared the totals (30 − 24 = 6). You must first divide each total by its time to get the rate (工作效率).
wrong.C: You found the difference of 1 correctly but picked the wrong person: Oliver's rate (6) is higher than Noah's (5).
wrong.D: Check the division: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 30 ÷ 6 = 5 — they are not equal.

questions.mistakes: Comparing totals instead of rates; mixing up who is faster.

questions.title: Find the time
questions.q: Mia packs 15 boxes per hour. How many hours does she need to pack 75 boxes?

wrong.A: You subtracted (75 − 15). To find time, divide the work by the rate.
wrong.B: You multiplied (75 × 15). Rate × time gives work, but here we already know the work — divide instead.
wrong.D: You added (75 + 15). Use time = work ÷ rate.

questions.mistakes: Multiplying, adding, or subtracting instead of dividing.

questions.title: Find the work done
questions.q: Ava draws 9 pictures per hour. She draws for 4 hours. How many pictures does she draw altogether?

wrong.A: You added (9 + 4). Each hour she draws 9, so it is 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 9 × 4.
wrong.C: You subtracted (9 − 4). Use work = rate × time.
wrong.D: You divided (9 ÷ 4). 9 is already the amount per hour; for 4 hours multiply.

questions.mistakes: Adding, subtracting, or dividing instead of multiplying.

questions.title: Remaining work
questions.q: Mr. Smith can mow a lawn alone in 5 hours. After he works for 2 hours, what fraction of the lawn is still left?
questions.explanation: Treat the lawn as 1. Rate = 1 ÷ 5 = 1/5 per hour. In 2 hours he finishes 2 × 1/5 = 2/5. Left: 1 − 2/5 = 3/5.

wrong.A: 2/5 is the part already done, not what is left. Remaining = 1 − 2/5 = 3/5.
wrong.C: 1/5 is his rate per hour, not the remaining fraction after 2 hours.
wrong.D: You inverted 2 and 5. Rate = work ÷ time = 1 ÷ 5 = 1/5, then remaining = 3/5.

questions.mistakes: Reporting the done part instead of the remaining; confusing rate with remaining work.

questions.title: Find the rate
questions.q: Noah baked 20 cookies in 4 hours. What is Noah's work rate in cookies per hour?
questions.explanation: Rate = work ÷ time = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cookies per hour.

wrong.B: You multiplied (20 × 4). Rate is work divided by time, not multiplied.
wrong.C: You subtracted (20 − 4). Use rate = work ÷ time.
wrong.D: You added (20 + 4). Divide the cookies by the hours.

questions.mistakes: Multiplying, adding, or subtracting instead of dividing work by time.

questions.title: Working together
questions.q: Mia paints 6 walls per hour and Oliver paints 4 walls per hour. There are 30 walls. If they paint together, how many hours will it take?
questions.explanation: Together their rate is 6 + 4 = 10 walls per hour. Time = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 hours. Check: Mia 18 + Oliver 12 = 30.

wrong.A: You used only Mia's rate (30 ÷ 6). When working together, add the rates first.
wrong.C: You subtracted the rates (6 − 4 = 2, then 30 ÷ 2). Working together means adding rates.
wrong.D: 10 is their combined rate per hour, not the time. Next step: 30 ÷ 10.

questions.mistakes: Using one person's rate; subtracting rates; stopping at the combined rate.
